name: vscode-to-explorer
description: Open files in their OS default application from the Explorer, run scripts, and open links in a chosen browser profile, powered by to-explorer.
author: John Haugabook

vscode-to-explorer.openAllFilesExternall.markdownDescription: Open **every** file double-clicked in the Explorer in its OS default application. When off, only the file types in `#vscode-to-explorer.fileExtensions#` open externally and code keeps opening in the editor.

vscode-to-explorer.fileExtensions.markdownDescription: File extensions (without a leading dot) that open in their OS default application when double-clicked. Has no effect when `#vscode-to-explorer.openAllFilesExternally#` is on.

vscode-to-explorer.openExternally.prompt.markdownDescription: When opening files externally, ask what to do with a double-clicked script instead of letting the OS run it. When on, a dialog offers **Execute**, **Open in VS Code**, or **Cancel**. When off, scripts open in the editor. Requires `#vscode-to-explorer.executeScript.enabled#` to offer **Execute**.

vscode-to-explorer.openExternally.pickAp.markdownDescription: When a file opened externally has no OS default application, show an "open with" picker to choose one. When off, the file opens in the editor as usual. Reliable on Windows; on macOS and Linux files are assumed to have a default application.

vscode-to-explorer.executeScript.enabled.description: Show an "Execute Script" entry in the Explorer context menu for executable script files.

vscode-to-explorer.executeScript.confirm.description: Show a confirmation dialog before running a script.

vscode-to-explorer.scriptExtensions.markdownDescription: Script extensions (without a leading dot) accepted by the "Execute Script" command.

vscode-to-explorer.browser.command.description: Browser command used when opening URLs in a profile (for example "chrome").

vscode-to-explorer.browser.useLastProfil.markdownDescription: Open URLs in the browser's last-used profile instead of a specific one. When on, `#vscode-to-explorer.browser.profile#` is ignored.

vscode-to-explorer.browser.openLinksInPr.markdownDescription: Route clicked `http`/`https` links through the configured browser and profile. Applies to links in Markdown, HTML, and plain-text files (Ctrl+Click) and to links in the rendered Markdown preview. When off, links open in the OS default browser as usual.

vscode-to-explorer.browser.profile.markdownDescription: Browser profile used when opening URLs. Examples: `Default`, `Profile 1`, or just `2`. Leave empty to open without selecting a profile.

vscode-to-explorer.terminal.enabled.markdownDescription: Handle Ctrl+Click on links printed in the integrated terminal through to-explorer. `#vscode-to-explorer.terminal.openWebLinksInBrowser#` and `#vscode-to-explorer.terminal.openFilesInDefaultApp#` choose which kinds of link are taken over; links that are not taken over keep VS Code's normal behavior.

vscode-to-explorer.terminal.openWebLinks.markdownDescription: Open `http`/`https` links clicked in the terminal in the browser and profile configured by `#vscode-to-explorer.browser.command#`, `#vscode-to-explorer.browser.useLastProfile#`, and `#vscode-to-explorer.browser.profile#` instead of VS Code's default link handling. Has no effect unless `#vscode-to-explorer.terminal.enabled#` is on.

vscode-to-explorer.terminal.openFilesInD.markdownDescription: Open file paths clicked in the terminal in their OS default application when their file type is listed in `#vscode-to-explorer.fileExtensions#` (or for every file when `#vscode-to-explorer.openAllFilesExternally#` is on). Scripts and other paths open in the editor as usual. Has no effect unless `#vscode-to-explorer.terminal.enabled#` is on.
